title: Is padded B4 causal-KL scoring worth adopting?
question: Does B4 padded batching make the real attention.causal_kl_v1 scorer materially faster than B1, and if the resulting head maps differ, does that difference matter downstream after the frozen recovery process?
_not_the_question: whether padded batching reproduces every intermediate top-k choice. That question was answered NO by the batch-invariance investigation and is not what adoption turns on.
_why_not: formal C3 is the causal-KL ATTENTION isolation experiment against B. This pilot decides an execution-protocol adoption question about the scorer that experiment would use. It shares the operator and nothing else: no C3 seed set exists, the confirmation battery is untouched, and no incumbent can be named here.
_arms_differ_only_by: the calibration_forward_batch_size in the causal step's hashed config. Same impl_id, same profile_id, same step label, same seed, same parent.
_arm_order_is_predeclared: FROZEN HERE, before either scorer runs. Whichever arm goes first pays for allocator growth and autotuning that the second does not, so the order is part of the protocol; choosing it after seeing the timings would be choosing the result.
_why_one: attempt 18 measured the frozen parent replay at ~24 minutes. A second replay can only reproduce the parent -- in which case it was redundant -- or fail to, in which case the pilot is over. Worse, it would let the two arms be compared against two DIFFERENT checkpoints that merely share a digest. One replay, one gated parent, both arms as verified suffixes from it, each re-identifying it from disk.

speed_gate.statistic: full causal scorer wall clock, B1 / B4
speed_gate._measured_not_inferred: from the two scorers' own synchronized clocks. NOT from FLOPs, NOT from the physical invocation count, and NOT from B1/B4 = 4.
speed_gate._fairness: before each timed scorer: the same verified parent is loaded, the same small untimed warm-up runs, CUDA is synchronized, and only then does the clock start. Same card, same pinned runtime, arm order predeclared before either result is read.

recovery_if_triggered._seed_scope: PILOT-ONLY. Not a historical A/B/C1/C2 recovery seed and not reusable as a formal C3 seed. There is NO formal C3 seed set.

may_not_produce: any change to DEFAULT_MICRO_BATCH_SIZE or to state identity semantics
_one_seed: a one-seed pair is not a statistical promotion test. It may report only descriptive paired differences; the maintainer chooses the formal C3 execution protocol afterwards.
artifact_lifecycle: Keep both scorer children until the adoption decision is secured. If recovery runs, keep both recovery checkpoints until recovery_search_v2 scoring and evidence are admitted. After terminal closeout a validly scored checkpoint with no remaining consumer needs its evidence retained and its weights may be removed, per the existing artifact policy.
